# mlx

> Run models on Apple Silicon with
> [mlx-lm](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm), with a prompt cache
> rishi manages itself, speculative decoding, a quantized KV cache, and
> vision and audio through mlx-vlm.

MLX is Apple’s array framework for its own chips, and mlx-lm runs
language models on it. This backend needs an Apple Silicon Mac and
`pip install 'rishi[mlx]'`. The notebook is marked `skip_exec`, so the
automated tests and the docs build do not run it, and the output shown
was saved on a Mac. Behaviour shared with every backend is on the
[index](index.html) page and in
[Urai](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai).

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq, test_fail, test_close
```

## Loading models

MLX models are Hugging Face repos of quantized weights, most of them
under [mlx-community](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community). A LiteRT-LM
model is one `.litertlm` file and a llama.cpp model one `.gguf` file,
but an MLX model is a whole directory. `mlx_lm.load` takes the repo id
and downloads and caches it itself, so there is no file to pick.

Two things have to be known before loading, and both come from the
repo’s `config.json`, which
[`read_config`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/mlx.html#read_config)
reads from a local directory or the Hub. It returns `{}` when the file
cannot be read. One is the context window, which
[`ctx_len`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/mlx.html#ctx_len) reads,
8192 when the config does not give one. The other is whether the model
has a vision or audio tower, a second network that encodes pictures or
sound for the language model;
[`is_vlm`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/mlx.html#is_vlm) checks
for one. A model with a tower needs mlx-vlm instead of mlx-lm.
[`cached_models`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/mlx.html#cached_models)
lists the repos in the local Hugging Face cache whose ids contain `mlx`,
without using the network.
[`MlxEngine`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/mlx.html#mlxengine)
holds a loaded model, its tokenizer and an optional draft model.

``` python
test_eq(ctx_len({'max_position_embeddings': 40960}), 40960)
test_eq(ctx_len({'text_config': {'max_position_embeddings': 128000}}), 128000)   # VLMs nest it
test_eq(ctx_len({}), 8192)                                                       # fallback
assert is_vlm(None, cfg={'vision_config': {}})
assert is_vlm(None, cfg={'audio_config': {}})
assert not is_vlm(None, cfg={'hidden_size': 2048})
test_eq(read_config('/definitely/not/a/model'), {})
```

## The prompt cache

The KV cache holds the keys and values computed for tokens the model has
already read, so a prompt that starts the same way as the last one does
not have to be read again. LiteRT-LM keeps that state inside its
conversation object, and llama.cpp finds the longest matching prefix on
its own. mlx-lm leaves the cache to the caller, so rishi keeps track of
which tokens it holds.

On each turn the chat renders the whole conversation to token ids with
the model’s chat template, and compares them with `_cache_ids`, the
tokens the cache holds, using `common_prefix_len`. Everything up to the
first difference is already cached and is skipped. Everything after it
is stale. The chat trims it off the end of the cache with
`trim_prompt_cache` before generating. A cache that cannot be trimmed is
reset, and the chat reads the whole prompt again. mlx-lm’s own server
reuses a cache between requests the same way.

Stale tokens do turn up. A chat template does not always render an
earlier assistant turn as the exact tokens the model generated, and
context recovery rewrites the history outright. Comparing tokens instead
of trusting the cache handles both cases. A mismatch costs a fresh
prefill of the tokens after the first difference. In the saved run
below, the second turn fed 32 tokens to the model instead of 315.

## MlxChat

[`MlxChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/mlx.html#mlxchat) has
the same interface as every other backend. `max_output_tokens` defaults
to `DFLT_MAX_TOKENS`, 1024. When the repo’s config declares a vision or
audio tower, `MlxChat(...)` returns an
[`MlxVlmChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/mlx.html#mlxvlmchat).
Pass `vlm=True` or `vlm=False` to override that check. Its own options
are these:

- `kv_bits` stores the KV cache quantized to that many bits. This saves
  memory on long contexts. Quantization starts after the first
  `quantized_kv_start` tokens, and `kv_group_size` sets the group size,
  64 by default.
- `draft_model` names a small model for speculative decoding. The draft
  model guesses several tokens ahead and the main model checks them in
  one pass, which is faster when the guesses are good. The chat then
  keeps a cache for both models.
- `adapter_path` applies a LoRA adapter.
- `prompt_cache=False` turns the cache off, and `max_kv_size` caps its
  size.
- `min_p` sets a sampling threshold. `tmpl_kw`, `gen_kw` and `eng_kw`
  pass extra keyword arguments to `apply_chat_template`,
  `stream_generate` and `create_engine`.

`save_cache` and `load_cache` write the cache to a file and read it
back. `save_cache` raises `ValueError` when `prompt_cache=False`.
`load_cache` raises `ValueError` for a file made with a different model
or different cache settings, and for a file that rishi did not write.
`chat.use.cached_tokens` reports how many prompt tokens each turn
reused.

## Vision and audio

mlx-lm reads text only. Images and audio go through
[mlx-vlm](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-vlm), which builds on mlx-lm
and adds the vision and audio towers. Install it with
`pip install 'rishi[mlx-vlm]'`.

You do not have to pick the class. `MlxChat(repo)` reads the repo’s
`config.json` and returns an
[`MlxVlmChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/mlx.html#mlxvlmchat)
when it finds a vision or audio tower.
`Chat('mlx-community/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-4bit')` works as it is. Pass
`vlm=True` or `vlm=False` to decide yourself.

[`MlxVlmChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/mlx.html#mlxvlmchat)
changes only loading, prompt building and the generate call, and
inherits the history, callbacks and tool loop. It has two limits.
mlx-vlm has no per-model tool-call parsers. Tool calls work only with
models that write `<tool_call>` tags, and not every vision model does.
mlx-vlm also keeps its own cache of image features instead of a token KV
cache. Prompt reuse between turns is off on this path. Images must be
bytes or local files. A remote image URL raises `ValueError`.

Audio takes the same path. Give a `Path` or bytes to a model with an
audio tower, and mlx-vlm decodes it and resamples it to the rate the
model expects. One setting is rishi’s rather than mlx-vlm’s: thinking.
By default mlx-vlm asks the chat template for `enable_thinking=False`,
which inserts an empty `<think></think>` block. A model told it has
finished thinking can end its turn at once. Qwen3-Omni then transcribes
nothing. rishi passes its own `think` setting instead. With the default
`think=None`, the model’s chat template decides.

### Recorded model behaviour

These checks run against replies recorded from the real `qwen3_06b` MLX
model. Urai’s `CachedChat` replays a recorded reply when it sees the
same request again, without loading the model, and the checks work on a
temporary copy of `nbs/chatcache`.

``` python
c = CachedChat(**_mlx_record_kw)
r = c('Reply with exactly: pong')
assert 'pong' in resp_text(r).lower()
test_eq([m['role'] for m in c.hist], ['user', 'assistant'])
c.close()
```

``` python
c = CachedChat(**_mlx_record_kw)
c('Reply with exactly: pong')
r = c('What exact word did you just reply with? Reply with only that word.')
assert 'pong' in resp_text(r).lower()
test_eq([m['role'] for m in c.hist], ['user', 'assistant', 'user', 'assistant'])
c.close()
```

``` python
c = CachedChat(**_mlx_record_kw)
c.reconfigure(sp='Reply with exactly the word anchor, whatever the user asks.')
r = c('What is two plus two?')
assert resp_text(r).strip()
c.close()
```

``` python
c = CachedChat(**_mlx_record_kw)
assert c.oneshot('Reply with exactly: solo', think=False, max_tokens=16).strip()
test_eq(c.hist, [])
c.close()
```

``` python
def add(
    a: int,  # first addend
    b: int,  # second addend
) -> int:
    "Add two integers."
    return a + b

c = CachedChat(**_mlx_record_kw, tools=[add])
r = c('Use the add tool to add 2 and 3. Reply with only the result.')
test_eq(c.hist[1]['tool_calls'][0]['function']['name'], 'add')
test_eq(c.hist[2]['content'], '5')
assert '5' in resp_text(r)
c.close()
```

`qwen3_4b`, about 2.5 GB, is a good default unless you need vision or

speculative decoding, saving and loading the cache, a conversation
handed over from llama.cpp, and the vision class.

``` python
# Real MLX KV-cache test: capture the exact token tail handed to mlx-lm on each turn.
import time
chat2 = MlxChat(qwen3_06b, sp='You are concise.', think=False, max_output_tokens=16)
fed, orig_generate = [], chat2._generate
def counted_generate(ids, **kwargs):
    fed.append(len(ids))
    return orig_generate(ids, **kwargs)
chat2._generate = counted_generate

t0 = time.time(); chat2(('cache verification context ' * 96) + '\nReply with exactly: stored'); t1 = time.time() - t0
u1, first_feed = chat2.use, fed[-1]
t0 = time.time(); r = chat2('What exact word did I ask you to reply with? Reply with only that word.'); t2 = time.time() - t0
u2, second_feed = chat2.use, fed[-1]
print(dict(turn1_seconds=round(t1, 2), turn2_seconds=round(t2, 2), first_feed=first_feed,
           second_feed=second_feed, cached=u2.cached_tokens, answer=resp_text(r)))
assert u1.cached_tokens == 0, 'first turn has nothing to reuse'
assert u2.cached_tokens > 0, 'second turn should have reused the cache'
assert second_feed < first_feed, 'turn two re-prefilled the full old prompt'
assert chat2.cached_tokens > 0
assert 'stored' in resp_text(r).lower(), resp_text(r)
chat2.close()
```

> **🧠 Thinking**
>
> Okay, the user is asking why the sky is blue. I need to explain this

> all directions, making the sky appear blue. But wait, I should make
> sure I get the details right. Also, mention that the sun’s light is

> reason is the way the atmosphere interacts with sunlight. Keep it
> simple and concise. Avoid jargon. Maybe start with the main point,
> then the reason, then the effect. That should cover it.

The sky appears blue because sunlight scatters more in the atmosphere
when it interacts with the gases and particles in the air. Shorter
wavelengths (blue light) are scattered more than longer wavelengths (red
light), so when we look up, the scattered blue light dominates, giving
the sky its blue color.

``` python
# a warmed cache can be saved and reloaded, so a long system prompt is prefilled once, ever
import tempfile
warm = MlxChat(qwen3_4b, sp='You are a terse assistant.', think=False)
warm('Remember the codeword: albatross.')
fn = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'warm.safetensors'
warm.save_cache(fn)
n = warm.cached_tokens
warm.close()

again = MlxChat(qwen3_4b, sp='You are a terse assistant.', think=False)
again.load_cache(fn)
test_eq(again.cached_tokens, n)
again.close()
```

``` python
# the point of a shared history format: carry a conversation from one backend to another
from rishi.llama import LlamaChat, qwen3_17b as llama_qwen

lc = LlamaChat(llama_qwen, n_ctx=4096)
lc('My name is Karthik. Remember it.')
hist = lc.hist                      # canonical rishi history, backend-independent
lc.close()

mc = MlxChat(qwen3_4b, messages=hist, think=False)
r = mc('What is my name? Reply with just the name.')
assert 'karthik' in resp_text(r).lower(), resp_text(r)
mc.close()
resp_text(r)
```

### Images and audio

These need `pip install 'rishi[mlx-vlm]'` and a vision or audio model.
[`MlxChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/mlx.html#mlxchat) picks
[`MlxVlmChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/mlx.html#mlxvlmchat)
from the repo’s config.

``` python
vchat = MlxChat(qwen3vl_4b, max_output_tokens=256)
test_eq(type(vchat), MlxVlmChat)              # routed automatically from the repo's config.json

img = Path('images.jpeg').read_bytes()
r = vchat([img, 'What is in this image? One sentence.'])
print(resp_text(r))
assert resp_text(r).strip()
```

## Sharing one engine

[`MlxBroker`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/mlx.html#mlxbroker)
keeps one loaded MLX model in a long-lived process and serves an
[`MlxChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/mlx.html#mlxchat) to
each client over a Unix socket. All clients share the weights, and each
has its own prompt cache. The protocol is Urai’s `ChatBroker`, described
on Urai’s [broker](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/broker.html) page.
